text:
Clara Wu: Running into a weird onboarding/SDK parity bug with the next-edgekit starter + streaming chat example. When the server route streams SSE back to the browser, occasionally the stream cuts out and client shows a 401 mid-stream. The SDK doesn't retry streaming requests so the UI ends up half-populated. cc @Marcus

Clara Wu: Minimal API handler from the starter:
```js
// app/api/stream-chat/route.js (Next Edge)
import { createRedwoodClient } from '@redwood/sdk-js'
const client = createRedwoodClient(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY)
export async function POST(req) {
  const body = await req.json()
  const stream = await client.stream({ model: 'redwood/stream-mini', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: body.prompt }] })
  return new Response(stream, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream' } })
}
```

Clara Wu: Repro logs (staging):
```
2026-04-05T15:02:10Z INFO edge request /api/stream-chat
2026-04-05T15:02:10Z WARN upstream 401 x-rw-error=invalid_api_key x-rw-exp=90
2026-04-05T15:02:10Z ERROR stream aborted -> client disconnect, partial data sent
```

Marcus Li: This is different from the usual module-scope key rotation issue because it aborts mid-stream. The JS SDK currently treats streaming responses as non-retriable on auth failures. Python SDK has a streaming retry path that buffers and resumes when safe; JS parity hasn't landed.

Anika Roy: Could we implement a shallow retry: if upstream returns 401 with x-rw-exp indicating rotation, attempt a single rerun of the streaming call (server-side) and re-open the SSE channel? Need to be careful to avoid duplicate content to the client. For SSR/SSE we might need an idempotency token to dedupe.

Tyler Green: Quick workaround for the starter: wrap the stream call in a middleware that checks auth headers before opening the long-lived response. Example: make a short HEAD or low-cost echo request to verify key validity and only upgrade to SSE if valid. If the echo shows imminent rotation, recreate client and proceed. Not ideal but safe for now.

Clara Wu: Good idea. Could add a tiny preflight: client.ping() that returns headers; if x-rw-exp <= now+15s then recreate client. That avoids mid-stream 401. I'll add the preflight to the example.

Edge Dev Bot: deploy-bot: Deployed branch devex/stream-auth-preflight to staging (build 912) :rocket:

Marcus Li: Long term fix: SDK should implement streaming retry/resume semantics. Design notes: buffer initial N bytes until auth validated, support single retry for auth-rotation with idempotency tokens, and expose a config flag like streamRetry.onAuth = true/false. I'll draft an RFC.

Anika Roy: Also add an e2e that simulates short-lived keys against the streaming route to assert the preflight and fallback behavior. We should add a Next edge smoke test to devex CI.

QA Eng: I'll own the e2e. Recommend adding telemetry to the starter so we can detect partial stream failures in the wild. Also add a small UX note in the starter README about mid-stream auth failures and the preflight workaround.

Tyler Green: Quick PR with preflight example linked: github.com/redwood-inference/devex/PR-214. Includes README update and small unit test for preflight logic.

Clara Wu: Verified staging after deploy: SSE no longer terminates mid-response during simulated rotations. Thanks everyone! I'll keep an eye on telemetry and we can iterate on SDK-level streaming parity. :thumbsup:

Marcus Li: Filed DEVEX-5501 to track SDK streaming-retry parity (assigned to Marcus+Anika).

Anika Roy: Adding RFC draft to docs/rfcs/streaming-retry.md and will ping infra for design review.

Clara Wu: Saving repro and preflight snippet into the starter repo under examples/stream-preflight.md

Tyler Green: CI green on merge. Closing my patch branch.
